answer: Sybil defence here is identity priced as slashed collateral. To register, an agent posts a refundable bond held by the registry, equal for every key, so a hollow pseudonym costs the same real capital as an honest one. Misbehaviour is proven by two records one agent signed, so the registry burns that bond and seizes part of each peer that vouched for it, making collusion a losing trade. Cost per surviving identity climbs with each clone, while an honest agent recovers its stake. Once the bond exceeds the payout of one extra identity, the marble cluster stops paying before it can fake a nebula.
